idiom_name: Map of mount/unmount view closures + replaceChildren switching + EventTarget change fan-out
implementation_notes: The DOM has no view objects, so the shortest real substitute is a registry module: a Map from view id to a record holding the element and its mount/unmount functions, one host element whose content is swapped with replaceChildren, and an EventTarget (or a Set of callbacks) for the model-change fan-out. This is idiomatic because closures already carry the view's state and the DOM nodes are the views - there is no class hierarchy to reproduce, and closing a view is unmounting plus dropping the reference. The classic structure is still justified when independent documents or panes must be tiled and activated together (MDI-style workspaces, browser-level multi-document shells); otherwise prefer a router (React Router's Outlet, the Navigation API) and let it own which view is current, keeping the registry for the state each route needs. When the swap has to be animated rather than instantaneous, document.startViewTransition() wraps the same replacement in a view transition.
pitfalls: A shared EventTarget keeps every listener of a still-listening element: views must unsubscribe on unmount (AbortController with { signal } is the shortest reliable way) or a closed view keeps reacting to model changes.

Keeping both a model reference in the registry and an element in the DOM creates the classic leak pair: removing the element and deleting the entry must happen in the same function, or the detached subtree and its closures stay reachable.

replaceChildren() destroys the replaced subtree completely - focus, scroll position, CSS transitions and uncontrolled input state vanish - so that state must live in the view's data and be reapplied on mount, or the old element must be hidden rather than removed.
A listener that re-renders synchronously on every mutation causes layout thrash under a burst of updates; coalesce with requestAnimationFrame or a microtask batch.
